title: Starter Blitz: SDK Onramp Lab Journal
content:
Goal:
A 30-minute, instructor-led "starter blitz" that gets a new engineer from zero to an instrumented, resilient SDK call in a local sandbox. Focus: fast feedback, observable signal for regressions, and a small set of failure-injection checks that exercise fallbacks.

Audience:
- New hires on eng-developer-experience and solutions eng.
- Customer engineers trying out Redwood SDK in an accelerated workshop.

High-level flow (30 minutes)
1) 0-5m — Warm up & credentials (fastest path)
   - Purpose: ensure network + creds work.
   - Scripted steps: set REDWOOD_API_KEY env, run `redwood whoami` shim (example below).
   - Success signal: CLI prints account id + quota summary.

2) 5-12m — Hello-generation: Minimal call + telemetry
   - Use minimal sample app (node/python) to call text generation with small prompt (<=50 tokens).
   - Ensure SDK emits span and token-cost metric.
   - Success: model returns a string, trace id appears in local logs, cost metric shows >0 tokens.

3) 12-20m — Local dev loop: simulate latency and caching
   - Flip a local flag to enable prefix caching. Re-run same prompt, observe reduced latency and token delta.
   - Exercise batching: run 5 parallel requests and observe batching telemetry in the console.
   - Success: median latency improves for cached request; batch size metric increments.

4) 20-28m — Resilience & fallback checks (failure injection)
   - Failure 1: throttle hosted API (return 429) — SDK should retry with exponential backoff and surface retry_count metric
   - Failure 2: model unavailable — automatic fallback to a smaller model variant (e.g., gpt-small) per routing policy
   - Failure 3: network partition — CLI toggles offline mode and verifies local stub returns cached replies or helpful error message
   - Success criteria: clear telemetry for retry attempts, fallback model name in span tags, and user-facing error that maps to recovery action.

5) 28-30m — Wrap & Next steps
   - Capture a sample alert/trace and attach to a quick bug ticket if anything broke.
   - Give the participant checklist for deeper exploration: dedicated capacity tests, private deployment checklist, and per-route observability.

Instructor props & prep (prework)
- A lightweight sandbox repo with: quickstart README, single-file examples (js/py), a local stub server to toggle errors, a tiny telemetry viewer (static HTML).
- Slack channel: #de-onramp-blitz with pinned links (confluence, GH examples, devtoken request).
- A single short deck: 6 slides covering the runtime constraints, what telemetry to expect, and safe failure modes.

Artifacts included in repo
- /examples/hello_generate.py and hello_generate.js (explicit env var checks + trace header capture)
- /tools/failure_injector.sh — toggles response codes on the local stub
- /telemetry/README.md — quick mapping of metrics -> dashboard names (latency_ms, token_cost, batch_size, retry_count, fallback_model)

Smoke test checklist (pre-run)
- env var REDWOOD_API_KEY set and can call account endpoints
- Node/Python runtimes installed (node 18+, python 3.10+)
- curl or httpie installed for stubbing checks
- local stub running on :8080 if offline scenarios are needed

Key commands (examples)
- whoami shim: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/account/whoami`
- quick generate (python): `python examples/hello_generate.py --prompt "Summarize this in 10 words"`
- enable failure injection: `./tools/failure_injector.sh set-429`

Telemetry assertions (must be visible in trainer console)
- trace.id exists and is logged alongside the request id
- metric: token_cost > 0 after generation
- metric: batch_size >= 1 when parallel requests executed
- attribute: fallback_model set when fallback occurs

Common gotchas & troubleshooting notes
- New users forget to export API key — include fallback messaging in CLI to link to devtoken page.
- Local IPv6 binding sometimes breaks the stub; prefer 127.0.0.1 in examples.
- Retry logic can mask a progressive error; instructor should show raw server logs when teaching.

Experiment matrix (quick, for follow-up)
- Variables: model variant (small/medium/large), sequence length (50/200/800), batching config (on/off), cache enabled (true/false)
- Metrics: p50 latency, p95 latency, token_cost per request, successful_fallback_rate, retries_per_request
- Quick hypothesis: enabling prefix cache reduces p50 by 20% for short prompts at small throughput.

Follow-up tasks (post-blitz, owners)
- Convert the lab into a self-serve GH Actions workflow (owner: Evan)
- Add a short screen-recorded demo to confluence (owner: Marina)
- Add assertions to the telemetry README and wire into CI smoke tests (owner: Ravi)

Notes to self / rough ideas (non polished)
- Could be 15-min microblitz variant — drop batching section and keep only hello+resilience.
- Might pair with a customer success run for low-touch onboarding: include pre-provisioned tokens with short TTLs.
- Consider a lightweight scoring rubric so attendees get a pass/fail badge for the workshop (helps internal metrics).

Attachment checklist for the doc
- Link to sandbox repo (pinned)
- Quick video (2-3 min) of the fallback flow
- Template bug ticket to file if telemetry mismatch (fields: trace id, request id, expected metric, observed)

Raw snippets to paste into examples
- python example (pseudo):
  import os
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  key = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=key, telemetry_enabled=True)
  resp = client.generate("Summarize X in 10 words")
  print(resp.text)

- node example (pseudo):
  const {Redwood} = require('@redwood/sdk')
  const client = new Redwood(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, {telemetry:true})
  const r = await client.generate({prompt: '...'})
  console.log(r.text)
notes: Informal journal style, iterate this into a lightweight self-serve lab next quarter. Keep conservative scope: 30m for instructor-led, 15m microblitz for async.
